The *Appasadda Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 13) is a training rule (*sekhiya*) from the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, translated by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *Being noisy* [SuttaCentral]. The rule forms part of the section of decorous conduct regarding quiet and restrained deportment within inhabited areas, and an English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

This training rule is widely attested across Buddhist monastic lineages. According to SuttaCentral, parallels are preserved in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, and both Parivāras, as well as in the corresponding Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Kāśyapīya, and Upāliparipṛcchā traditions in Pali, Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral].
